Adjusted assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- The intermeeting 50 bp cut and liquidity operations (T-bill purchases, repos, IOER/ON RRP settings) signal rising downside risks from COVID-19 despite “strong fundamentals,” already a slightly negative tone.
- SLOOS adds a credit headwind: banks reported tighter standards and other terms on C&I loans, reduced credit limits, and increased credit score thresholds. Standards also tightened for construction and land development loans, with weaker demand reported in that segment. Consumer loan conditions were mixed (some categories unchanged, some tighter), with credit card/consumer demand often unchanged to weaker.
- Forward-looking SLOOS responses are notably cautious: banks expected tighter lending standards in 2020 across riskier categories (including C&I, multifamily CRE, construction/land development), reduced risk tolerance, and deterioration in loan portfolios and collateral values.
- Taken with FSR-noted vulnerabilities (elevated valuations, high corporate leverage, and funding market fragilities), SLOOS suggests monetary easing may transmit less effectively through a tightening bank channel, modestly darkening the overall policy signal.

Net: Shift the tone from slightly negative to more clearly negative given concurrent tightening in bank lending standards and cautious expectations.
